answer: An attested-execution mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring every agent to run in a trusted environment that reports a measurement of its kernel configuration to the network. A remote verifier checks the report against registry records and issues credentials only when the kernel hash is unique. Since the hardware key cannot be exported, fifty identities require fifty machines, with real hardware costs. A scheduler prunes duplicates like a garden, while audit counters, accurate as marble ledgers, flag credentials sharing one key and slash their stakes.
